newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-MUSHTAQ SHRUGS OFF JET LAG TO SNAP UP 7-24.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MUSHTAQ SHRUGS OFF JET LAG TO SNAP UP 7-24.

text.p: Leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed snapped up a match-winning seven for 24 for Somerset at Taunton on Friday just 24 hours after he arrived from Pakistan's tour of Sri Lanka.
Mushtaq turned down the chance of missing the game to rest and, despite heavy strapping on his right leg, bowled Somerset to a comprehensive 221-run victory over Ireland in the Benson and Hedges Cup.
The Irish, who had beaten an English county in the 50 overs competition for the first time earlier this week, were routed for 128 in the face of Somerset's imposing 349 for seven.

Mushtaq struck with his second delivery to have Hansie Cronje lbw, a vital blow as the South African captain had played a key role with an unbeaten 94 in Ireland's historic Cup success over Middlesex on Tuesday.
The Pakistani wrist-spinner baffled the Irish with his googly as their last seven wickets tumbled for 57, only opener Andrew Patterson resisting with the top score of exactly 50.
Mushtaq's Pakistan skipper, Wasim Akram, marked his first appearance of the season for his adopted county Lancashire with a telling all-round performance to keep the holders in the Cup.
Akram struck Lancashire's top score of 52 not out from 73 deliveries, then captured two for 54 to help snatch a last-ball victory over Warwickshire at Edgbaston.

Lancashire won by losing fewer wickets after the scores were level. The holders scored 208 for eight, South African fast bowler Allan Donald taking five for 25, and dismissed the home county for 208 in exactly 50 overs.
After being beaten in their first two group A games, Lancashire's win kept alive their hopes of qualifying for the quarter-finals, though they need to win their remaining two matches.
There was also a pulsating climax at Derby where both Yorkshire and Derbyshire scored 260 for seven, the visitors getting the verdict by virtue of their higher run rate over the first 25 overs.
Fast bowler Chris Silverwood rescued Yorkshire after almost giving the match away when his last delivery of the contest was ruled a no-ball.
That left Derbyshire requiring only two to win but former England paceman Phil DeFreitas was restricted to a single to leave the scores tied.
But Yorkshire took victory on the count-back ruling after 25 overs when they had scored 116 for two against Derbyshire's 103 for two.
Kent made it three wins out of three in group C as pace bowler Dean Headley led the way in overwhelming Sussex by six wickets at Canterbury.

Headley's brilliant new ball spell of 10-5-14-2 sent Sussex sliding to 18 for three. They were subsequently 60 for six, and only reached 153 thanks to a maiden limited-overs half-century from tailender Paul Jarvis.
The top two teams in the four groups qualify for the quarter-finals.
